articles.title: Lance Broadway Dies at 43, Former Mets Pitcher Was Actor After MLB Career
articles.summary: Former MLB pitcher Lance Broadway was pronounced dead on Tuesday, according to the Dallas County Medical Examiner public information records. A cause of death has not been revealed.
articles.body:
Former MLB pitcher Lance Broadway was pronounced dead on Tuesday, according to the Dallas County Medical Examiner public information records . A cause of death has not been revealed.

Broadway was drafted by the Chicago White Sox in the first round of the 2005 MLB draft (No. 15 overall) and made 19 appearances and two starts for the team across three seasons (2007-09), going 2-2 with a 4.69 ERA, 1.56 WHIP and 30 strikeouts in 40.1 innings.

He then pitched part of the 2009 season with the New York Mets, going 0-0 in eight appearances with a 6.75 ERA, 1.70 WHIP and nine strikeouts in 14.2 innings.

After his MLB career he transitioned to acting, with film roles in Olympus Has Fallen , True Tales and Beyond the Trek and guest appearances on shows such as Saint George , Kevin from Work , Lucifer , Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D. and Colony .

articles.title: President Donald Trump announces he's posthumously pardoned Pete Rose, who was reinstated by MLB last spring
articles.summary: When MLB commissioner Rob Manfred removed all deceased players from the league's permanently ineligible list in May 2025, a path to the Baseball Hall of Fame...
articles.body:
"I have just given a Complete and Total Pardon to the Late, Great Pete Rose, a true Baseball SUPERSTAR & LEGEND," Trump said in his post.

Trump's announcement of the posthumous pardon comes more than a year after MLB commissioner Rob Manfred acknowledged that the president partially played a role in Rose's MLB reinstatement , which finally made MLB's all-time hits leader eligible for the Baseball Hall of Fame.

In 1990, Rose — a 17-time All-Star and three-time World Series champion — entered guilty pleas to two counts of filing false tax returns. He confessed to failing to report $354,968 over the course of four years, as reported by The Associated Press. That went down not even a year after he was permanently banned from baseball in the wake of an investigation that found he bet on the Cincinnati Reds while playing for and managing them from 1985-87.

Ultimately, in July 1990, as chronicled by the AP, Rose was sentenced to five months in prison, fined $50,000 and ordered to conduct 1,000 hours of community service. He was reportedly instructed to perform that service as part of a one-year probation period, working with inner-city children in Cincinnati as a gym teacher's assistant.

Rose also ended up repaying the Internal Revenue Service, according to the AP.

He finished his MLB career with 4,256 hits. For reference, the next closest player on the career hits leaderboard is Ty Cobb, who was inducted into the Hall as part of its inaugural class in 1936 after he piled up 4,189 hits .

Rose spent 19 seasons with the Reds, with whom he won a pair of World Series rings. He won it all one final time while playing for the Philadelphia Phillies. That championship arrived in 1980 amid his five-season stay with the club. Rose began the 1984 season with the now-defunct Montreal Expos before returning to Cincinnati. Nicknamed "Charlie Hustle," he ended his MLB playing days with 2,165 runs scored and a pair of Gold Glove Awards for his feats in the outfield.

Rose was NL Rookie of the Year in 1963. He was NL MVP in 1973 and then World Series MVP two years after that in 1975.

Along the way, he won three NL batting titles. Additionally, he holds the record for most MLB games ever played with 3,562 to his name. During the six seasons he managed the Reds (1984-89), he registered a combined 412-373-1 record.

articles.title: White Sox, Rockies Make Surprise Luis Castillo Trade, Full Details Revealed
articles.summary: The Colorado Rockies announced they acquired Chicago White Sox starting pitcher Luis Castillo in a trade on Thursday.
articles.body:
The Colorado Rockies announced they acquired Chicago White Sox starting pitcher Luis Castillo in a trade on Thursday.

The Rockies received Castillo and right-hander Davis Martin from the White Sox in exchange for pitcher Sean Sullivan and catcher Douglas Veliz.

ESPN's Jeff Passan reported the Rockies will take on Castillo's entire salary.

Castillo has 10 years of MLB experience as well as three All-Star nods under his belt, although he's coming off a 2026 campaign in which he failed to meet expectations.

He started the year with the Seattle Mariners, but recorded a 5.06 ERA while allowing 107 hits in 99.2 innings of work before he was traded to Chicago ahead of the deadline.

Castillo didn't fare any better with the White Sox, posting an 8.42 ERA across nine appearances following the swap.

The Rockies will hope that the 33-year-old can look like his former self in 2027, as he owned a 3.39 ERA while averaging 9.3 strikeouts per nine innings from 2022-25.

Castillo will earn $24.2 million next year (via Spotrac ). He also has a $25 million vesting option for 2028 if he reaches 180 innings pitched during the 2027 season.

Martin started 28 games for Chicago in 2026, compiling a 9-8 record to go along with a 3.95 ERA and 1.315 WHIP.

The 29-year-old excelled down the stretch of the regular season, putting together a 1.71 ERA across his final five games.

As for Sullivan, he appeared in five contests for the Rockies during his rookie season. He's listed as Colorado's No. 20 prospect, via MLB Pipeline .

Sullivan gave up 22 earned runs in 22.1 innings pitched during his time in the majors last season, although he owned a 3.14 ERA across 18 starts with Double-A Hartford in 2025.

Veliz is 17 years old and recently suited up in 29 games during the Dominican Summer League. He hit .300 with seven doubles and 16 RBI.

articles.title: Rockies reportedly acquiring RHPs Luis Castillo, Davis Martin in trade that sends White Sox pair of prospects
articles.summary: Colorado is taking on the full salary of Castillo, a three-time All-Star, according to an ESPN report.
articles.body:
The Colorado Rockies have finished with MLB's worst ERA five seasons in a row. Their altitude problem isn't going anywhere, but they're hoping to improve their pitching situation this offseason.

They took a step toward doing so on Thursday night, according to multiple reports , which detailed Colorado acquiring right-handed starters Luis Castillo and Davis Martin in a trade with the Chicago White Sox.

Castillo is a three-time All-Star. The Rockies are taking on his full salary and sending two prospects to Chicago in the deal, per ESPN's Jeff Passan .

One of those prospects is left-hander Sean Sullivan, according to MLB.com's Mark Feinsand. Sullivan, 24, debuted this past season for the Rockies, struggling with an 8.87 ERA over five starts.

Castillo, who will be 34 next season, is coming off a down year and reportedly due more than $24 million in 2027.

The Seattle Mariners dealt him to the White Sox ahead of the trade deadline during the 2026 campaign. But Castillo wound up making just six starts for an upstart Chicago team that went on to win its first playoff series since 2005.

Castillo, previously an All-Star with the Mariners and Cincinnati Reds, was left off the White Sox's postseason roster. Not too far removed from helping Seattle reach the ALCS in 2025, he'll reportedly get a fresh start in Colorado.

Martin, 29, pitched only one inning for Chicago during its head-turning playoff foray. In the regular season, however, he was a mainstay in the White Sox rotation.

He started 28 games, registering a career-best 3.95 ERA and 122 strikeouts. Martin piled up at least seven Ks in six outings, maxing out with 10 in a May 4 win over the Los Angeles Angels.

articles.title: New MLB Rumors Unveil Mets' Interest Level in Ty France Amid Padres Free Agency Buzz
articles.summary: The New York Mets have interest in free agent first baseman Ty France, per Jon Heyman of the New York Post.
articles.body:
The New York Mets have interest in free agent first baseman Ty France, per Jon Heyman of the New York Post .

However, the San Diego Padres want to re-sign France, per Heyman, who added that the Pittsburgh Pirates, Cleveland Guardians, Arizona Diamondbacks, Milwaukee Brewers and Chicago White Sox "all make sense too."

The 32-year-old France has played eight MLB seasons. He enjoyed a career-best campaign in 2026, hitting .295 (.865 OPS) with 21 home runs and 72 RBI over 133 games for a 91-win Padres team that reached the National League Division Series.

The Mets need a first baseman after letting Pete Alonso walk in free agency to the Baltimore Orioles during the 2025-2026 offseason. Alonso, a five-time All-Star and two-time Silver Slugger, led the American League with 43 home runs and 113 RBI in 2026.

The Mets missed Alonso's production. Per MLB.com , New York finished third-last in baseball with a .667 OPS and sixth-last with a .231 batting average. The Mets' 18 home runs (24th) and 77 RBI (23rd) also paled in comparison to most of MLB.

New York finished last in the National League with a 74-88 record. First base must be addressed for the Mets to get out of the cellar.

France is certainly an option, though it'll cost the Mets. Spotrac places his market value at three years and $49.3 million ($16.4 million per year). The potential competition for his services might make it difficult as well.

Ultimately, New York will be in the race for his services. New York has also reportedly met with representatives for corner infielder Alec Bohm at the general manager meetings last week, per Ken Rosenthal and Will Sammon of The Athletic. The 30-year-old Bohm, who has played all seven of his seasons with the Philadelphia Phillies, hit .249 (.698 OPS) with 15 home runs and 88 RBI last season.

articles.title: New Tarik Skubal Rumors Reveal Padres' Status in MLB Free Agency Sweepstakes Amid Mets Buzz
articles.summary: The San Diego Padres reportedly are getting in on the race for Tarik Skubal.
articles.body:
The San Diego Padres reportedly are getting in on the race for Tarik Skubal.

Per Jon Heyman of the New York Post , the Padres met in person with the free-agent pitcher on Wednesday, making them the fourth team to do so. Heyman added that a fifth undisclosed team also met with Skubal this week.

Heyman noted that San Diego isn't the favorite to land Skubal, but added that "ultra-aggressive Padres GM A.J. Preller and uber-committed new ownership give them a shot to upset" teams like the New York Mets, Toronto Blue Jays and Los Angeles Dodgers for Skubal.

Heyman also reported that the Padres are interested in their starter from last year, Michael King, as a "fallback option" in free agency.

According to Heyman, the "expectation" is that Skubal will make a free agency decision before the expected lockout begins on Dec. 1 at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Skubal, who will be 30 on Friday, started last season with the Detroit Tigers before being traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers at the deadline. The two-time Cy Young winner went 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA, a 0.96 WHIP and 186 strikeouts.

articles.title: Mets sign reliever Darwinzon Hernandez to three-year, $12 million deal
articles.summary: The 30-year-old lefty spent the last four seasons in Japan.
articles.body:
The Mets and left-handed reliever Darwinzon Hernandez have agreed to a three-year, $12 million contract, according to reports .

The 30-year-old Venezuelan last pitched in the majors four years ago, appearing in 91 games for the Red Sox from 2019 until 2022. During that time, despite flashing nasty stuff and striking out a lot of batters, he struggled mightily with walks, walking close to eight batters per nine innings and posting an ERA north of five over 85 1/3 innings for his major league career. The Red Sox designated him for assignment in January of 2023 and he had a short stint in the Orioles organization before being released in July of 2023.

Hernandez then signed with the Fukuoka SoftBank Hawks of Japan's Nippon Professional Baseball, where he has pitched the past four season with greatly improved results. During his time in NPB, he has put up a 2.46 ERA in 131 2/3 innings, struck out close to a third of the batters he has faced, owning the second-highest strikeout rate in NPB among relievers since 2024 . Most importantly, he lowered his walk rate to 8%, which is less than half of what it was during his time in Boston. Hernandez features a four-seam fastball, a slider, and a curveball.

Alex Speier of The Boston Globe recently reported that Hernandez was looking to return to MLB this season and the Mets, in need of arms, are giving him that chance. The deal , which is still pending a physical, includes a $500,000 signing bonus, a $4 million salary for 2027, and a $3.75 million salary in each of the two subsequent years.

articles.title: With Major League Baseball's lockout looming, would the league's proposal 'fix' baseball?
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers' World Series win over the Tampa Bay Rays challenges claims a salary cap would fix competitive balance in Major League Baseball.
articles.body: Barring a miracle, we are less than two weeks away from a prolonged work stoppage in Major League Baseball. The Collective Bargaining Agreement between the 30 team owners and the MLB Players Association expires in early December, and the two sides, despite some bargaining between them, are no closer to a deal than they were when negotiations started over the summer. If anything, they might be further apart. NEW STATEMENTS FROM ROB MANFRED, MLBPA, GUARANTEE BASEBALL IS SHUT DOWN INDEFINITELY IN TWO WEEKS The disagreement stems from the creation of a salary cap, which MLB has avoided for decades, despite other sports like the NBA and NFL implementing their own cap systems years ago. Many fans have, for some inexplicable reason, come down on the side of the owners, believing that limiting what players can earn will somehow "level the playing field," as the league's propaganda campaign has claimed. While there would be a so-called "floor" under the league's proposal, it would again be far less than the cap. Meaning that the cheaper small-market teams already raking in tens of millions of dollars per year in revenue sharing would still spend as little as possible on player payroll. MLB OWNERS ARE BACK WITH A NEW SALARY CAP PROPOSAL TO SHUT DOWN SPORT EVEN AFTER BREWERS WIN WORLD SERIES If money is such a pivotal factor, the proposed ~$80 million gap would still allow teams that try to win to sign at least three or four big-name star-level players that the cheaper teams wouldn't. Not to mention that free agents, with their earnings now artificially limited to make owners richer, would gravitate towards the larger markets like LA, New York, Chicago or Boston anyway, as those cities would offer more lucrative off-field opportunities. Along with a broader commitment to winning, or trying to win, that the Pirates and Marlins of the world laugh at. All these issues aside though, the argument that pro-cap fans make is that while the owners might want a cap for the wrong reasons, the outcome would be beneficial. Competitive balance would be restored, they say, because of a limit on big spending teams. So it's worth examining then, is that claim actually true? Obviously, we just completed a 2026 season in which the Milwaukee Brewers, long one of baseball's cheapest organizations, won the World Series in historic fashion. They went 11-2 in the playoffs, with their two losses coming by a combined total of just two runs. One in walk-off fashion. They were three outs away from becoming the first team to sweep the NLCS and World Series. That NLCS sweep came against the Los Angeles Dodgers and their $400 million+ payroll. The Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays in the World Series, another one of baseball's cheapest teams. Yet the Rays have made the World Series three times since 2008 and twice since 2020. Here's how that compares to some of baseball's biggest markets over the last decade: The Rays have been a more successful organization at reaching the World Series over the past decade than every big market team other than the Dodgers and Houston Astros. Interesting. The San Diego Padres, who have spent a fortune signing players like Fernando Tatis Jr., Manny Machado, Xander Bogaerts, Yu Darvish, Joe Musgrove, Jackson Merrill, rank in the top five in overall spending in the last five seasons. They have one win in the NLCS to show for it and no World Series appearances. Still, there are many who remain convinced that a cap would ultimately make a substantial difference in outcomes, relative to the capitalist market baseball currently enjoys. Thankfully, The Athletic put that theory to the test. And got what might be surprising results for some fans. Eno Sarris, one of their baseball writers, used regression analysis to "determine the state of competitive balance." His methodology "incorporated three ways of measuring market size — payroll, Nielsen’s ranking of television markets and a metric the union and league created called "market score" — and examined the correlation between those factors and outcomes on the field." He then compared the current state of baseball to the NBA and NFL, the two salary capped leagues. And while there's a lot to unpack, here's the topline, as the article states: "First, the math largely supports the Players Association’s position that baseball’s competitive balance is already strong." "Second, MLB’s vision for a competitive-balance utopia might not level the playing field the way fans expect," it adds. There is a caveat; sustained spending over time can correlate, at least somewhat, with higher winning percentages in the regular season. But the complaints about "big markets" are mostly false, they found. "If, instead of payroll, the analysis uses 'market score' — a metric that factors in TV audiences, population and median household income — then market size explains almost nothing statistically about how a team will fare." Analytics and modern front offices have also closed the gaps between teams, their analysis found, and the postseason is mostly random, making regular season success of little value. "In addition, when compared to the past, team win-loss records are more clustered in the middle, with fewer clubs occupying the extremes," the article reads. "At the same time, outcomes in the playoffs also remain much more random than those in the regular season." As for a salary cap, even the league's top executives admit that it will do little-to-nothing to create more playoff appearances for small-market teams. Morgan Sword, an executive VP and one of commissioner Rob Manfred's top economics experts, told The Athletic, "No, no, I don’t think it would (lead to more playoff appearances), and I don’t think it needs to." Welp. There goes the marketing campaign. They also found that the gaps between teams is smaller than it's been in decades, thanks to the latest CBA, which increased revenue sharing and luxury tax penalties, giving smaller market teams more money for existing. But what about the most "important" thing; does spending more money buy more wins? Well, they found that over the past five seasons, payroll "accounted for 17 percent of the variance in a team's winning percentage in a single season." In actuality, it correlates to a similar relationship between "team wins and how many ground balls a team's pitchers induce." In other words, yeah, it doesn't matter very much. Then there's market size. Their analysis also found that "Market score explains just 1 percent of the variance in MLB wins." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! During this current five-year CBA, 24 of 30 teams made the playoffs. Of the six that didn't, three each came from big and small markets. Sure sounds like competitive balance, doesn't it? You can also compare outcomes between baseball, the NFL, and NBA. Payroll doesn't matter much in the NFL, because the cap and floor are so close, but the outcomes between all three sports are similar anyway. Baseball actually has more parity because it's harder to reach the postseason than it is in the other leagues. 80% of MLB have reached October in the past five years, 78% of the NFL, 90% of the NBA. 38% of MLB's bottom half payroll teams have reached the postseason, while it was 54% in the NFL and just 28% in the NBA. But again, it's harder to make the postseason in baseball, because only 12 of 30 teams get to October. The NFL and NBA are trophies for everyone leagues, which makes the results far less impressive. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER There is no relationship between market size and playoff outcomes, they found, and the minimal relationship between payroll and postseason success is entirely because of one team: the Dodgers. "If the Dodgers were removed from the calculation, there would be no statistically significant relationship since 2022 between payroll and playoff winning percentage," the article explains. Before going into what this all means, it's worth revisiting one quote from Rays starter Drew Rasmussen about the Brewers. After the series, he told reporters that they were "the best team I've ever played at the Major League level." OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Are the 2026 Brewers the best baseball team ever? No, and they may or may not have been the best baseball team in 2026. But the point is that over a small sample size, like a postseason or postseason series, any playoff team can be "the best team" the opposition has ever played. That's what makes baseball so unpredictable. It's more prone to hot streaks and cold streaks than any other. So what's the takeaway here? A salary cap would not "fix" baseball, because there's nothing to fix. Spending money helps, a little, when it comes to winning more games in the regular season. It doesn't matter, at all, when it comes to reaching or winning the World Series. The Dodgers' wins were down to the same factors as any other championship team: a combination of talent, timing, and luck. Which is why they've reached the postseason 17 times since 2008 and have failed to win a title 14 of those times. The relationship between payroll and winning percentage is akin to the advantage a team gets from having a lot of groundball pitchers. Which is to say, not much. It's easy, and lazy, to say that you can "buy" a championship. You can't. If you sustain higher levels of spending for years, you can have a small advantage with a regular season winning percentage. You will buy yourself no advantage whatsoever in the postseason. The fact that owners have convinced fans of something that is not true is devastating not just for the fans who refuse to learn accurate information, but because they are using that support to justify an extended shutdown. That's a disaster. And even worse, it's an unnecessary one.

articles.title: Ranking MLB's Potential 2026-27 Free Agents Who Are Non-Tender Candidates
articles.summary: The non-tender deadline marks the annual decision each MLB team faces on whether to offer or "tender" a contract to the arbitration-eligible players on their roster. Teams have until 5 p.m. ET on Friday to make those decisions.
articles.body:
The non-tender deadline marks the annual decision each MLB team faces on whether to offer or "tender" a contract to the arbitration-eligible players on their roster. Teams have until 5 p.m. ET on Friday to make those decisions.

If they tender a contract, the team and player can continue to negotiate a salary figure for the upcoming season in an effort to avoid an arbitration hearing. If they do not tender a contract, the player is considered to be "non-tendered" and immediately becomes a free agent.

Outfielder Adolis García was the biggest name cut loose at the non-tender deadline last year, while JJ Bleday, Jonah Heim and Nathaniel Lowe are a few of the other non-tendered players who ended up providing solid value.

Ahead is a look at the top non-tender candidates, and this article will also serve as a ranking of the top players who are ultimately non-tendered once news starts trickling in on Friday.

Non-Tender Candidates (Position Players)

1. OF Jarren Duran, BOS 2. OF Jo Adell, CLE 3. OF Brandon Marsh, PHI 4. 1B Jake Burger, TEX 5. 2B Ernie Clement, TOR 6. 1B Spencer Torkelson, DET 7. IF Royce Lewis, MIN 8. OF JJ Bleday, CIN 9. 1B/OF Gavin Sheets, SD 10. 2B Matt McLain, CIN 11. 3B Nolan Gorman, STL 12. 1B/3B Mark Vientos, NYM 13. 1B Triston Casas, BOS 14. IF/OF Matt Vierling, DET 15. OF Josh Lowe, LAA

A hefty projected salary is the driving factor behind Jarren Duran ($11.1 million), Jo Adell ($9.6 million), Brandon Marsh ($8.3 million) and Gavin Sheets ($6.5 million) appearing on this list. The most surprising non-tender of that group would be Adell, who played well after he was acquired by the Guardians at the trade deadline, but that organization loves to pinch pennies.

With a 108 OPS+, 28 home runs and 90 RBI in 2026, Jake Burger was as productive as anyone on this list, but his lack of secondary value outside of what he does in the batter's box limits his value. Spencer Torkelson and Nolan Gorman offer similar power upside with little to prop up their profile if they're not slugging.

There might not be two more obvious change-of-scenery candidates than Triston Casas and Mark Vientos , who both looked like offensive cornerstones just a few short years ago. They are both still only 26 years old, making it easier to buy the idea of untapped upside.

With a 4.47 ERA over 131 innings, Bailey Ober was a productive back-end option for the Twins last season, but his $6.9 million projected salary and the recent addition of Sonny Gray could lead to Minnesota cutting ties.

Luis Gil won 2024 AL Rookie of the Year, Ronel Blanco had a 4.7-WAR season and threw a no-hitter that same year and Josiah Gray was an All-Star in 2023, but all three pitchers have fallen out of their respective teams' rotation plans.

Camilo Doval (66 G, 4.15 ERA, 9.8 K/9) and Garrett Cleavinger (51 G, 4.79 ERA, 11.8 K/9) should be able to secure MLB contracts, while Lucas Erceg (52 G, 13 SV, 5.59 ERA) has enough high-leverage experience to be an appealing buy-low candidate.

articles.title: “Imagine Claiming a Pitcher Waived by Mets” – Fans React to Cubs Acquiring 28-year-old DFA’d Pitcher
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs have claimed 28-year-old right-handed pitcher Chayce McDermott off waivers from the New York Mets in the 2026-27 MLB offseason. No correspon...
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs have claimed 28-year-old right-handed pitcher Chayce McDermott off waivers from the New York Mets in the 2026-27 MLB offseason. No corresponding roster move was required, since Chicago already had open spots on its 40-man roster after protecting prospects ahead of the Rule 5 Draft.

McDermott spent the 2026 season with the Baltimore Orioles, Los Angeles Dodgers and Mets. He posted a 5.87 ERA in 7.2 innings in five appearances. In his MLB career, he holds a 1-1 record and a 10.18 ERA across 10 appearances, including two starts.

Fans shared their thoughts on the latest acquisition by the Cubs.

"Imagine claiming a pitcher who was waived by the Mets. LOL," one fan wrote.

Several more fans came up with sarcastic remarks:

These reactions make it clear that Cubs fans are not happy with this acquisition. Chicago fans expect major moves this offseason from the front office after being eliminated in the 2026 wild-card round during the postseason.

The Cubs may have acquired McDermott due to his strikeout potential in the minor leagues. In six seasons, he has posted a 25-27 record with a 4.31 ERA, 625 strikeouts, and 278 walks in 445 innings pitched.

McDermott is out of minor-league options, according to CubsHQ . That means Chicago cannot freely send him between the majors and minors without exposing him to waivers.

Cubs Take Interest In Japanese Triple Crown Winner

The Cubs need a couple of outfielders this offseason after Seiya Suzuki, Ian Happ, Michael Conforto, and Tyrone Taylor became free agents this winter. Currently, they have Pete Crow-Armstrong, Matt Shaw, Pedro Ramirez, and Kevin Alcantara in the outfield room.

The Cubs have reportedly taken an interest in Japanese slugger Teruaki Sato to address their outfield depth, per Patrick Mooney of The Athletic . Sato was posted by the Hanshin Tigers on November 1. Therefore, he has until Dec. 16 to sign with an MLB team.

The Japanese 6-foot-1 slugger hit .277/.345/.579 with 40 home runs, 34 doubles, four triples, 102 RBI, and 10 stolen bases in 139 games in 2025 to win the Central League MVP award. Last season, he won the NPB Central League Triple Crown after hitting .306/.383/.609 with 39 home runs, 40 doubles, three triples, 106 RBI, and eight stolen bases in 143 games.

After the Cubs saw a lot of success with Japanese stars in Wrigley Field, with Seiya Suzuki and Shota Imanaga, it won't be a surprise to see them make a play for Sato.
